entities.summary:
Croesus (b. 595 BCE) was a king of the ancient Anatolian kingdom of Lydia, known for his vast wealth and his reputation as a wise and just ruler. He was a key figure in the Greco-Persian Wars, serving as the satrap of Lydia during the Persian Empire's expansion into Asia Minor. His reign was marked by significant cultural and economic achievements, including the establishment of a powerful and centralized state, the development of a sophisticated system of law and governance, and the promotion of trade and commerce throughout the region.










Croesus was also known for his role in the famous oracle of Delphi, which foretold his death at the hands of his own son. According to legend, Croesus's son, Atys, was instructed by the oracle to kill his father, and Croesus's subsequent death at the hands of his own son was seen as a fulfillment of the prophecy. This event marked the beginning of the end of the Persian Empire's expansion into Asia Minor, as the kingdom of Lydia was eventually conquered by the Greeks.


















Croesus's legacy extends far beyond his own lifetime, as his policies and achievements had a lasting impact on the development of Western civilization. His emphasis on law and governance, for example, influenced the development of constitutional monarchy in Europe, while his promotion of trade and commerce helped to establish the foundations of modern capitalism.
